body:
**The year the account carries a death.** 2018 opens, on New Year's Day, with a
four-tweet thread about Dan's 97-year-old great-grandmother, her advanced
dementia, and two days in which all of it briefly went away. It is the first
time in ten years this feed does sustained, serious, first-person family
testimony, and it is the best single piece of writing on the account.

The rest of the year is the Trump-era reading list, a caregiving load he
quantifies once, and — in October — the first negative word about Opie.

## 1 January: terminal lucidity, watched and documented

> *"For the past few months I've been 'watching' my (surprisingly capable)
> 97-year old great grandmother who is physically healthy, but lives alone with
> advanced dementia. She's a real card and a huge influence in my life, and
> she's fiercely independent"*
>
> *"I've witnessed her mental capabilities diminish and as time passed, her
> personality/'soul'/etc was less pronounced. It happened gradually, and the
> degree to which it was happening became harder to see, as it became common
> place to anyone who spent regular time with her"*
>
> *"Recently communication has been near impossible, and basic function
> becoming difficult. But, out of nowhere, when she woke up yesterday...her
> memory, speech, physicality, stamina, and appetite returned and this
> continued for a second day today"*
>
> *"I put this video together to show how extreme the change was. I've since
> read a bunch about terminal lucidity and I've def not ruled that out, nor do
> I think this could or would be anything more than extremely temporary. But
> it's one of the most peculiar things I've ever seen"*

Four things are happening in that thread at once, and they are the whole
person.

**He is a carer.** *"For the past few months"*, and on **22 January**,
*"I've spent 70 hours at grams in the past week"* — a quantified load, stated
in passing inside a joke about something else.

**He noticed the thing that is hard to notice.** The second tweet is an
observation about *observation*: the decline was hidden precisely from the
people closest to it, because gradual change resets the baseline daily. That is
anomaly detection turned on his own perception, and he states the mechanism
before stating the event.

**He documented it, then found the literature.** He made a video for the
comparison, and *"I've since read a bunch about terminal lucidity"* — the
technical term for the phenomenon, found afterwards. Encounter the anomaly,
record it, then go and learn what it is called: the method
`CONTEXT_CORE_EXPANDED` describes as *"domain-invariant 'find where it breaks'"*
applied to his great-grandmother's dying.

**And he refuses to over-claim it.** *"I've def not ruled that out"* is not the
same as a diagnosis, and *"nor do I think this could or would be anything more
than extremely temporary"* forecloses the consoling reading in the same
sentence he offers the extraordinary one. He is twenty-nine, writing about the
best possible news, and he will not let himself have it.

She is almost certainly the *"ratchet great grandma"* who was *"the country
club Queen Bee in 1960"* (2014-05-27) — the same woman, twice, four years
apart, in two completely different registers.

## The Resistance reading list, read in public

2018 is the year the *"voracious reader"* ambition (11 April: *"my goal in life
is to one day be described as a 'voracious reader'"*) starts being enacted, and
what he reads is exactly of its moment.

**Michael Wolff's *Fire and Fury*** — bought on publication weekend (6 January,
*"I haven't even gotten to the first chapter but the preface and authors note
are explosive"*), progress reported (8 January, *"I'm at the Scaramucci
chapter"*), and then a real observation on the 8th: *"Notably absent in
#FireAndFury is Mike Pence... his lack of presence in the larger, more defining
moments described in the book is pretty telling. He is, if nothing else,
diligently committed to his political future."* That is a reader noticing what
is **missing** from a book rather than reacting to what is in it.

**James Comey's *A Higher Loyalty*** — pre-ordered and chased through Audible
support (17 April), then, before it arrived, a correction to himself: *"been so
excited for 'a higher loyalty' that i got clap'd by @AriMelber and his
surgically-accurate unpacking of comey's partisan blunders. i'm no less hyped
for the book, but i've got better perspective."* And a review at the halfway
mark (18 April): *"a solid, engaging yet slow read."*

Both books are Resistance-liberal artefacts, which continues 2017's finding
exactly: the politics of this period are anti-Trump institutionalism, not the
left. So does **15 February**, on gun control: *"imagine, if you will, a
@realDonaldTrump with the EXACT same problems but with a progressive approach
to gun control... what a wasted opportunity"* — Trump conceived as a wasted
*vehicle*, which is a thought only available to somebody who still believes the
vehicle matters more than the direction.

## 29 October: "opie sucks though"

Three words, in a year with eighty-nine posts, and they are the first negative
statement about Opie or Anthony Cumia anywhere in the archive.

Set against [[wiki/self/twitter/2014]]'s *"nothing but love and respect ant"*
(4 July 2014) and the 2022 retrospective, this is the **middle term of the
sequence the corpus was missing**: 2014 supportive → **2018 dismissive** → 2022
narrating it as radicalisation. The change is real and it is gradual, and it
begins somewhere between 2014 and 2018 rather than at the firing.

Note what is not here. There is no argument, no explanation and no politics in
it — just *"opie sucks though"*, appended to something else. The affiliation
drops before the reasons for dropping it are ever stated, which is the same
shape as the Republican exit in 2009 and the neo-atheism exit in 2013.

## The self-descriptions, which are unusually direct this year

- **25 February**: *"i'd rather be in front of a crowd of 5,000 people, than in the middle of a room with 500... mostly just because i'd have something to do other than mingle and be a spoilsport non drinker buzzkill."* The only place on the account he names his own sobriety, and he names it as a social liability rather than an achievement.
- **2 April**: *"i don't have a moral compass but i make up for it by role playing as a regular, decent human being sometimes."*
- **20 March**: *"found out that i have terminal whiteness after i started keeping a running spreadsheet of the words and phrases from @desusandmero that i want to incorporate into my vocabulary."* A spreadsheet. For vocabulary. Reported as a joke and almost certainly true, which makes it the earliest documented instance of the systematising instinct this entire wiki is a product of.
- **7 December**: *"I'm 30 years old, got a Misfits tattoo last week, and my fb cover photo is the logo for a soccer team. A sport which I have never watched. Pretty excited to have now accomplished 100% of the items on my 1st grade 'what I want to be when I grow up' list."*

## Texture

A 23andMe swab sent before Christmas and lost by USPS (27 December), which
follows the coat of arms of October 2017 — two dated attempts at ancestry in
fifteen months. *Mario Kart 8 Deluxe* bought *"as a girlfriend game"* and
enjoyed (19 March). A theory that the Stormy Daniels NDA connects to Larry
Flynt's offer for presidential dirt (31 January), which is conspiracy-shaped
reasoning offered with its mechanism attached and a named funding source —
the version of the habit [[wiki/mind/synthesis/vertical-authority-skepticism]]
distinguishes from crankery. And on 22 January, filed without comment inside a
joke: *"mom told me she joined tinder."*

## What would change this reading

The great-grandmother thread is quoted here in full and interpreted heavily;
the interpretation is mine and the thread is short. The identification with the
2014 *"country club Queen Bee"* is an inference from two posts and a
relationship, not a stated fact. And *"opie sucks though"* is three words —
treating it as a turning point is reasonable only because the archive is
complete enough here to say nothing earlier says anything like it.
